title: Compatibility of the dual and Tate data
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions]: $X_0$ is smooth, separated and of finite type over $k_0$, geometrically connected of pure dimension $d\geq0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and its structure morphism is exceptional-adjoint admissible. Use $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ and the geometric-Frobenius automorphism $g_\gamma$. Let $(K,\varphi_K)$ be a strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect over $\Lambda_X$ [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x]. At finite level strict means [def-trf-strict-weil-complex]; at integral and field stages use the realized normalized-system, localized and common-stage strict data of [def-pur-tate-datum]. Put $K^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\Lambda_X)$ [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x], and let $r\in\mathbf Z$.

The contragredient datum $\varphi_{K^\vee}$ and twisted datum $\varphi_{K^\vee(r)}$ of [def-pod-dual-tate-datum], interpreted at these coefficient stages, make $K^\vee$ and $K^\vee(r)$ strict Weil complexes. The coefficient evaluation
$$K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}K^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_K}\Lambda_X$$
is a morphism of Weil objects. The canonical identification
$$\mathbb D_XK\xrightarrow{\sim}K^\vee(d)[2d]$$
of [thm-sf-dual-perfect] is an isomorphism of Weil objects, with the canonical purity orientation and its Weil datum as in [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace]. All these objects and morphisms commute with finite reduction, adic normalization, rationalization, finite coefficient-field extension, and idempotent splitting; at algebraically closed coefficients the splittings exist by [lem-weil-weil-complex-qbar-idempotent-complete].

proof.text: Write $P=Lg_\gamma^*$, $H(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom_X(M,N)$, and $e_{M,N}:M\otimes^LH(M,N)\to N$. The coefficient dual and evaluation mean [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x]. By [lem-pod-coefficient-dual-perfect], $K^\vee$ is perfect and belongs to $D^b_{ctf}$ at every stated stage. The automorphism is the scheme isomorphism of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], not absolute Frobenius. At finite level [thm-trf-internal-hom-pullback] applies with $M=K$ (site-perfect by [def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x]) and $N=\Lambda_X$ (the coefficient unit). At integral level, and on its field-stage images, [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation] supplies $c:PH(K,\Lambda_X)\simeq H(PK,P\Lambda_X)$ with its actual evaluation identity. Thus the first arrow of the contragredient composite is an isomorphism at all stages, not merely an operation defined on objects. In what follows use its tensor-Hom transposition and shift compatibility as well. The current [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] specifies its first arrow as $\alpha$ of [lem-pod-geometric-frobenius-internal-hom-comparison]. For $M=K,N=\Lambda_X$ that lemma applies at all stages: $K$ is site-perfect and both inputs are finite-Tor constructible. Its $\alpha$ and the comparison $c$ just used are the transpose of the same pulled-back evaluation under the same tensor comparison, hence equal by the adjunction bijection. Thus the proof uses exactly the arrow of the current definition.

source.place: Step 1: isomorphism and domain of the coefficient dual

proof.text:
Set $a=\varphi_K:PK\simeq K$ and $u=\varphi_\Lambda:P\Lambda_X\simeq\Lambda_X$. The definition [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] is $\varphi_{K^\vee}=H(a^{-1},u)c$. All three arrows are invertible, so this is a strict datum, by [def-trf-strict-weil-complex] at finite level and [def-pur-tate-datum] at the other stages. Here is the evaluation square explicitly. Naturality of evaluation gives
$$e_{K,\Lambda_X}(a\otimes H(a^{-1},u))=u\,e_{PK,P\Lambda_X},$$
since precomposition by $a^{-1}$ cancels $a$. Compose with $1\otimes c$ and the tensor comparison $\mu$ of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. The evaluation identity in [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation] gives
$$e_{K,\Lambda_X}(a\otimes\varphi_{K^\vee})\mu=uP(e_{K,\Lambda_X}).$$
This is exactly the morphism condition for evaluation. The argument uses finite and integral comparisons, with localized/common-stage images, and does not apply the rational-only operation lemma at finite coefficients.

source.place: Step 2: explicit cancellation in the Frobenius evaluation square

proof.text: For any $r\in\mathbf Z$, [def-pur-tate-datum] supplies the invertible Tate datum $\tau_r$ with geometric-Frobenius scalar $q^{-r}$; $q$ is a unit since $\ell\ne p$. By [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], the actual structure map on $K^\vee(r)$ is $(\varphi_{K^\vee}\otimes\tau_r)\mu$, a composite of isomorphisms, exactly the tensor convention of [def-pod-dual-tate-datum]. Twisting preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ by [prop-weil-twist-preserves]. It also preserves perfectness here: locally the twist line is the coefficient unit, so a bounded finite-projective model for $K^\vee$ remains such a model. This proves the strictness assertion without any rational-only operation theorem.

source.place: Step 3: tensor datum and its bounded perfect domain

proof.text:
Apply [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace] to $f_0=a_{X_0}:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ and input $\Lambda$ on the point. The Poincare conventions [def-pod-conventions] give smoothness, separated finite type, pure relative dimension $d$, the admissible structure morphism, and the prescribed coefficient stage. The constant coefficient object has its canonical strict datum. The theorem says that the smooth purity map $\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\simeq\omega_{X,\Lambda}$ is equivariant; its inverse $\eta_X$ is therefore equivariant too. Its internal Hom is in the required domain by [thm-sf-dual-perfect]. Equip $H(K,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$ with $H(a^{-1},\varphi_\omega)c$. Naturality of $c$ in [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation] gives
$$H(K,\eta_X)H(a^{-1},\varphi_\omega)c=H(a^{-1},\tau_d[2d])c\,P(H(K,\eta_X)).$$
Thus applying internal Hom to the actual purity orientation is equivariant. No base-change square or claim that geometric Frobenius is a $k$-morphism is used.

source.place: Step 4: the orientation and its internal-Hom map

proof.text: Put $T=\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$. The twist interchange in [thm-sf-dual-perfect] is the inverse of the canonical evaluation comparison $\alpha:K^\vee\otimes^LT\simeq H(K,T)$. Its transpose is coefficient evaluation tensored with $1_T$, followed by the unit isomorphism. Step 2 makes the evaluation equivariant; Step 3 supplies the Tate datum, and [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] preserves tensor associativity and units. The transposition identity of [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation] therefore makes $\alpha$ equivariant. The shift comparison in that lemma identifies the structure on the source with $\varphi_{K^\vee}(d)[2d]$. Consequently $\alpha^{-1}\circ H(K,\eta_X)$ is an equivariant isomorphism. It is precisely the canonical identification $\mathbb D_XK\simeq K^\vee(d)[2d]$ specified by [thm-sf-dual-perfect], so this proves the claimed identification for its canonical maps.

Let $C$ be finite reduction $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,n}$ with $m\geq n$, integral reduction, or rationalization. By [lem-fix-operation-reduction], its pullback, tensor and internal-Hom comparisons preserve actual evaluations, units and associativity; the finite-quotient Hom assertion applies because $K$ is site-perfect. Write $v_C:C H(K,\Lambda_X)\simeq H(CK,C\Lambda_X)$ for the Hom comparison. Apply $C$ to the equation of Step 2. Under those comparisons it becomes the evaluation equation for $CK$ and the candidate dual datum obtained by conjugating $C(\varphi_{K^\vee})$ by $v_C$. Precompose its first input by $\varphi_{CK}^{-1}$. The tensor-Hom transpose bijection of [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation] then identifies that candidate with $H(\varphi_{CK}^{-1},\varphi_{C\Lambda})c$. Thus $v_C$ is a Weil morphism, and evaluation is carried to evaluation. The tensor comparison commutes with $\mu$ by [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], and the Tate data are coefficient-stage data of [def-pur-tate-datum]. Applying the same calculation with $\Lambda(d)[2d]$ in place of $\Lambda$, and the finite-reduction/scalar compatibility in [thm-sf-dual-perfect], proves compatibility of the canonical purity-duality identification. This uses a transpose characterization of specified maps, not an assertion that all maps are automatically compatible.

For adic normalization use the actual normalized reduction system of [def-pur-tate-datum]. In [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] the output system datum is specified by applying $\mathcal R_X$ to the integral contragredient and twist composites and their inverse arrows; its evaluations are their finite reductions with the quotient cocycle. Use these specified system arrows here. The functor $\mathcal R$ and the evaluation-defined comparison $\beta$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] are maps in derived system categories and preserve evaluation, transposes and composition. Pullback, coefficient tensor and the corresponding evaluation words act on these systems by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. In particular apply the cancellation $a^{-1}a=1$ from Step 2 in that category to the given realized isomorphism $a$, not to separately chosen level maps. This proves the same evaluation equation as a system identity. The integral comparison of [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation] is its functorial realization. The exact isomorphism inverse image preserves products and limits by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image], so it preserves the product-cone differential $1-s$ as well. Taking this functorial derived limit therefore preserves the already constructed equality and its inverse maps. The integral Tate datum in [def-pur-tate-datum] is realized in this same system sense. This proves compatibility with adic normalization; it never deduces equality of integral morphisms merely from equality of all their reductions.

source.place: Step 5: coherent adic realization, not a levelwise equality test

proof.text: For $E\subset L$ of ramification index $e$, use the cofinal levels $A_{E,n}\to A_{L,en}=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_L$. The comparisons of [lem-coef-finite-free-extension] preserve evaluation, commute with reduction, and are natural under the geometric-Frobenius scheme isomorphism. Hence the calculation of Step 6 applies to these specified scalar comparisons. For their completed realizations use Step 7 and the natural, identity- and tower-compatible integral isomorphisms of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]; its Hom and tensor comparisons are the coefficient-stage operations being used. Rationalization carries the equations to $E\to L$. Naturality holds on localized Hom groups, including arbitrary rational Weil isomorphisms and their inverses. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, represent the finitely many objects, maps, inverse equations and equivariance equations over one finite field as in [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], enlarging once for each required equality in the colimit Hom groups. Compatibility under further extension makes these representatives independent of that choice. The Tate and purity-duality comparisons use [def-pur-tate-datum] and [thm-sf-dual-perfect]. Thus every comparison and identity descends with its prescribed Frobenius datum.

source.place: Step 5: finite-field extension and common-stage descent

proof.text:
Finally let $h:K\to K$ be an equivariant idempotent, and choose a splitting $L\xrightarrow{i}K\xrightarrow{p}L$, $pi=1$ and $ip=h$. At the common algebraically closed stage such splittings in the Weil category exist by [lem-weil-weil-complex-qbar-idempotent-complete]. Contravariance gives the splitting $L^\vee\xrightarrow{p^\vee}K^\vee\xrightarrow{i^\vee}L^\vee$ of $h^\vee$, since $i^\vee p^\vee=(pi)^\vee=1$. Give $L^\vee$ the datum $H(\varphi_L^{-1},\varphi_\Lambda)c$; [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation] needs no perfectness of $L$, and its naturality in the first variable makes these arrows equivariant. Evaluation naturality gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_K(i\otimes p^\vee)=\operatorname{ev}_L(1\otimes pi)=\operatorname{ev}_L.$$
At rational/common stages, [lem-coef-rational-retract-evaluation] also gives restriction of the perfect coefficient pairing; for a given splitting at finite or integral stages, the displayed naturality equation itself identifies the restricted evaluation. Twisting sends the splitting to $i\otimes1,p\otimes1$ by functoriality. If $I_K:\mathbb D_XK\simeq K^\vee(d)[2d]$ is the canonical map, its restriction is
$$I_L=i^\vee(d)[2d]\,I_K\,\mathbb D_X(p).$$
Its inverse is $\mathbb D_X(i)I_K^{-1}p^\vee(d)[2d]$; the two products are identities using $pi=1$, $h^\vee=p^\vee i^\vee$ and the naturality $I_K\mathbb D_X(h)=h^\vee(d)[2d]I_K$ of [thm-sf-dual-perfect]. It is equivariant as a composite. If $L$ is perfect, naturality for $i,p$ makes $I_L$ its canonical map; perfectness of $L$ is not used. These formulas prove preservation of the actual splitting and restricted maps, including $h=0$ and $h=1$, rather than merely existence of some splitting. The same formulas apply whenever a splitting is given at another stage, and scalar extension preserves them by Steps 6–8.

source.place: Step 5: inclusion/projection formulas for idempotent splitting

blueprint_update.statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions of this chapter (the fixed setting), let $(K,\varphi_K)$ be a strict Weil complex with $K$ perfect. The datum $\varphi _{K^\vee }$ of [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] defines a strict Weil complex $(K^\vee ,\varphi _{K^\vee })$, the coefficient evaluation

$$
K\otimes ^L_{A_X}K^\vee \xrightarrow {\  \operatorname {ev}_K\  }A_X
$$

is a morphism of Weil objects, the twisted object $(K^\vee (r),\varphi _{K^\vee (r)})$ is a strict Weil complex, and the canonical identification $\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee (d)[2d]$ of [thm-sf-dual-perfect] is an isomorphism of Weil objects (the compatibility of the purity isomorphism with the geometric-Frobenius data is the Weil equivariance of purity and trace, [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace], and the duality isomorphisms are morphisms of Weil complexes by [lem-fix-weil-operations]). All these objects and morphisms commute with finite reduction, adic normalization, rationalization, finite coefficient-field extension, and idempotent splitting (which exists for Weil complexes by [lem-weil-weil-complex-qbar-idempotent-complete]).

proof.text:
Step 1: $\varphi _{K^\vee }$ is a genuine Weil datum, i.e. a typed isomorphism of the displayed source and target. The first arrow of the composite in [def-pod-dual-tate-datum] is the canonical isomorphism

$$
Lg_\gamma ^*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,A_X) \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } R\mathcal Hom_X\bigl(Lg_\gamma ^*K,Lg_\gamma ^*A_X\bigr),
$$

the derived internal Hom under the pullback along the geometric-Frobenius automorphism of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], which is an isomorphism by the exactness of the pullback along an automorphism and the functoriality of the internal Hom, recorded in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; the second arrow is induced by the canonical datum $\varphi _A$ on the constant object, the canonical structure of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]; and the third by $\varphi _K^{-1}$. Each is an isomorphism, hence so is the composite, and it is a structure map of one object $K^\vee$, so $(K^\vee ,\varphi _{K^\vee })\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ by the definition of the strict Weil complex of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], the underlying object $K^\vee$ lying in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ by [lem-pod-coefficient-dual-perfect]. Step 2: the evaluation is equivariant. The evaluation is the counit of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction of [def-weil-derived-tensor], whose unit–counit identity is natural; the definition of $\varphi _{K^\vee }$ is precisely the typed iso making the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc} Lg_\gamma ^*\bigl(K\otimes ^L_{A_X}K^\vee \bigr) &  \xrightarrow {\  \sim \  } &  Lg_\gamma ^*K\otimes ^L_{A_X}Lg_\gamma ^*K^\vee \\ \big\downarrow \varphi _K\otimes \varphi _{K^\vee } &  \sim &  \quad \  \sim \quad \big\downarrow \operatorname {ev}_K\\ K\otimes ^L_{A_X}K^\vee &  \xrightarrow {\  \operatorname {ev}_K\  } &  A_X \end{array}
$$

commute, by the naturality of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] (the composite being the image of the identity under the unit–counit of the adjunction carried through the three isomorphisms), so the evaluation is a morphism of Weil objects by [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Step 3: the twisted object: $\varphi _{K^\vee (r)}=\varphi _{K^\vee }\otimes \tau _r$, the tensor of two Weil data, is a Weil datum by the compatibility of the derived tensor product with the pullback along $g_\gamma$, of [def-weil-derived-tensor] and [lem-fix-weil-operations], and $\tau _r$ is the equivariant structure of the Tate line of [def-pur-tate-datum] with normalization $q^{-r}$. Step 4: the purity identification: $\mathbb D_XK\cong K^\vee (d)[2d]$, of [thm-sf-dual-perfect], is an isomorphism of Weil objects by the Weil equivariance, [thm-pur-weil-equivariance-of-purity-and-trace], of the purity map and of the trace, together with the naturality of internal-Hom evaluation under the automorphism pullback in [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Step 5: the transport statements: all the constructions are those of the operations of the six-operations package, whose coefficient comparisons are built from the same evaluation and tensor maps and are preserved by the automorphism transport of [lem-fix-weil-operations]; and the data are built from the same operations, so they commute with these transports.

Reuses the existing coefficient comparison and coherent-system nodes; no duplicate coefficient-change lemma is introduced. Repair of the subsequent landing refusal: rebased on the current DAG, re-read the changed def-pod-dual-tate-datum and its newly named comparison, identified its alpha with the evaluation-normalized comparison by the adjunction bijection in Step 1, used the specified realized output-system arrows in Step 7, and refreshed all affected verbatim citations.
split_report.blueprint: Current blueprint proof Steps 1–5: delivered Steps 1–2 realize contragredient and evaluation, Step 3 Tate twist, Steps 4–5 purity identification, Steps 6–9 reduction, normalization, rationalization, field extension and splitting. The unit sk-def-weil route is unchanged.

tool_uses.why: Underlying coefficient dual lies in the required perfect finite-Tor constructible domain.
Finite-coefficient isomorphism for a site-perfect first variable; definition of the operation does not prove invertibility.
Generic monoidal pullback comparison and its coefficient coherence; does not replace the contragredient route.
Rank-one twist preserves bounded finite-Tor domains, needed to type the strict twisted object.
Geometric purity orientation is equivariant, applied only to the smooth structure morphism and the coefficient unit.
Canonical underlying purity-duality identification and its evaluation and coefficient normalization.
Actual tensor/Hom/evaluation coefficient comparisons on the finite site-perfect and integral domains.
Coherent system maps for evaluation, transposes and reduction/limit; avoids an unjustified equality test by finite evaluations.
Actual inverse-image, tensor and evaluation maps on derived systems, including their transposes.
Exact equivalence preserves products and limits in the functorial adic realization.
Finite field-extension scalar Hom comparison and its Frobenius/evaluation normalization at cofinal ramified levels.
Natural integral operation/scalar comparisons with identity and tower coherence.
Existence of a Weil-category splitting; the proof separately computes the induced dual and evaluation maps.
Perfect coefficient pairings restrict to adjoint rational retracts; existence of splittings alone says nothing about evaluation.

New node lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation: true. At finite level g^{-1} is an equivalence of ringed topoi; at integral level RHom of D^b_c objects lies in D^b_c by cor-coef-integral-internal-hom; at the field stages the rational category takes no Karoubi completion, so its objects are integral objects. Tested on g=id, M=Lambda, N=0, shifts, and a rank-one point object (gives scalar b^{-1}). It is statement-only and restates no clause of the item. The existing lem-pod-geometric-frobenius-internal-hom-comparison is a special case of it (site-perfect first variable), not a duplicate. The new node is needed in Step 9, where the retract L is not known to be site-perfect. Step 1 identifies alpha with c because both are transposes of P(ev)mu^{-1}. Steps: I checked hypotheses and types. Step 2's evaluation cancellation holds; Step 4 applies thm-pur-weil-equivariance with f_0=a_{X_0}, K=Lambda, using no base-change square and not treating g_gamma as a k-morphism; Steps 6-8 use lem-fix-operation-reduction (site-perfect first variable), R_X functoriality as specified in def-pod-dual-tate-datum, and the A_{E,n}->A_{L,en} levels; Step 9's retract formulas check out. It is an equivariant isomorphism using only naturality of I_K for h, and it agrees with L's own canonical map only when L is perfect. The corrected item is under fixes/.
